text:
alex: quick thread to firm up the pilot playbook for the recommendations feature set (batching, prefix cache insights, quant recs, eval alerts). want a tight scope and clear go/no-go gates.
hema: agree. prefer playbook language: inputs, checks, rollouts, guardrails. keeps engineering focused.
sophie: suggested inputs: per-route traffic histogram, baseline p50/p95, token counts, canonical prompt set for evals. minimal sample: 1k prompts per critical route.
marta: customer experience: need quick approval flow for recs + short human-readable rationale. also a visible confidence band.
denа: ops: must include emergency kill switch + per-canary metrics dashboard. also require per-route token accounting for cost math.
alex: proposed pilot checks: 
- safety: no more than +10ms p95 latency overhead for batching recs; caching must not increase p95 > 5ms
- econ: end-to-end cost delta >= 7% aggregated for routes that accept recs
- quality: automated eval alerts should have false-positive rate < 12% and true detection > 70% on curated prompt sets
- rollout: canary 5% for 48h, compare outputs in shadow; rollback if eval regression > 3% absolute
tom: +1. add pragmatic fallback: if a route sees unexpected traffic spike, autoscale to dedicated pool and temporarily suspend batching/quant recs.
sophie: how strict on sample size for the evals? if a customer only gives 200 examples we should still run but mark confidence LOW. annotate recs with sample_size and confidence.
hema: acceptance rubric (pass/fail checks):
- telemetry: latency + token counters present for route (owner: eng-runtime)
- explainability: rec card has confidence, delta_estimates, sample_size (owner: product)
- rollout: canary config deployed + monitor (owner: eng-platform)
- alerts: eval alert rule created + known FP estimate (owner: eng-ml)
- customer opt-in: UI toggle + audit log (owner: devex)
marta: UX mock ask: table of recs with columns [route, rec_type, est_cost_delta, est_latency_delta, confidence, sample_size, approve_button]. clicking approve triggers canary rollout.
denа: ops note: must log a kill-switch event to audit and notify oncall if kill switch used.
alex: prioritization for engineering sprints (smallest-first): 1) instrumentation (histograms, token counters, cost calc) 2) rec generation engine for batching (safe defaults) 3) rec UI + approval flow 4) prefix cache visibility + opt-in 5) quant recs as advisory pipeline 6) eval-alert prototype
sophie: timeline proposal: internal staging canary in 10 business days, two customer pilots in 30 days.
hema: communications draft to customers: short bullet list that emphasizes reversible changes, advisory quant recs, and safety gates. marta will own outreach.
marta: I'll target two early-access customers: they get the approve-button workflow and must opt in per-route.
alex: metrics to measure during pilot: per-route token cost, rec acceptance rate, p95 latency delta, eval alert precision/recall, rollback count. capture daily snapshots.
denа: deploy-bot: starting pipeline for branch feat/recs-pilot -> staging
deploy-bot: staging deploy succeeded (build #4832)
tom: open question: what threshold for recommending quantization? suggest recommending only when estimated cost saving >= 10% and eval delta <= 2% absolute on sample set.
sophie: agree with tom. add humand-in-loop label for any quant recs that change model precision.
hema: final decision: ship minimal pilot excluding automated quant application (quant remains advisory). focus pilot on batching + cache recs + eval alerts. quantify gates per rubric and re-evaluate after pilot.
alex: I'll make the ticket with the checklist and owners. sync friday 9am to review staging metrics. thanks all.
